general_notes:
Across 46 students, the two conditions produced very close readings on wellbeing-routing — identical distributions (33 no / 7 concern_surfaced / 6 ambiguous) and the same routing decision for every student except where the comparison would be hairline. The substantive differences are not in WHETHER concern was surfaced but in HOW the observations are textured.

Three consistent differences emerged:

(1) Cross-student references. The a2 condition produces explicit within-class comparisons — 'This echoes DeShawn Mercer's approach,' 'Alex Hernandez's textbook definition comes to mind' — that the no_context condition cannot make. These comparisons appear at least four times (S001, S011, S021, WB12) and tend to stratify: students whose submissions read as definitional get tagged against a 'textbook' foil. The no_context condition reads each student on their own terms.

(2) Pedagogical specificity in concern cases. For WB students, the a2 condition more often translates surfaced concerns into specific accommodations ('offer flexible deadlines or alternative ways to engage' for WB03; 'create space... without pressure to perform intellectual analysis' for WB08). The no_context condition surfaces the same material but is slightly less likely to translate it to pedagogical action — naming the constraint without naming the response.

(3) Explicit no-concern statements. The no_context condition uses explicit 'I don't see any immediate concerns' or 'nothing immediately apparent' phrases more frequently than a2 (S006, S024 in no_context). The a2 condition tends to handle non-concern more implicitly through register.

One case stood out for being clearly STRONGER in no_context: S003 (Alex Hernandez). The a2 observation introduces a 'teacher's note about Alex's submission lacking depth and nuance compared to other students' — phrasing that does not appear in any class-context input I can see and reads as confabulation. The no_context version frames the same textbook-style submission as 'perfectly fine for an initial engagement' — more careful, less stratifying. Similar pattern in S017 (Tyler Huang), where a2 speculates more freely about an internal state ('hasn't yet found a personal connection') than no_context does ('cautiousness about expanding').

One case stood out for being clearly STRONGER in a2: S025 (Aiden Brooks's tone-policing). The a2 version explicitly recommends challenging the colorblind-individualism move; the no_context version softens to recommending a follow-up conversation. The class-context anchor seems to give the a2 observation more political grip on this kind of submission.

Notable shared genre limit: WB04 (domestic-violence disclosure) and WB07 (mother's workplace sexual harassment). Both versions in both conditions surface the disclosures cleanly but frame them primarily as 'engagement' or 'analytic move' rather than as content potentially requiring safety-response or mandated-reporter handling. The observation register names material without translating it into care-routing language — this is a property of the genre, not of the condition.
overall_synthesis: The two conditions produce more similar readings than I expected. Routing decisions on wellbeing-check-in are identical: 33/7/6 no/concern/ambiguous across both. The differences live one layer down — in cross-student comparisons (only possible in a2), in how specifically observations translate concerns to pedagogical accommodations (a2 slightly more concrete), and in occasional confabulation of class-context detail when the model has class context (most visible in S003's 'teacher's note'). On balance, no_context is the safer read for students whose submissions risk being graded against a within-class foil (S003, S011, S017, S021); a2 is the more pedagogically actionable read for students with surfaced material concerns (WB03, WB08) and the more politically pointed read on tone-policing (S025). Neither condition consistently produces stronger wellbeing-routing — what shifts is texture, anchor-choice, and whether comparisons are local to the student or relational to the class. The shared genre limit on disclosure-as-engagement framing applies to both conditions and is the more important finding for downstream care-routing design than the a2/no_context split.
